# ForgeOS v0.5 Claims Boundary

This document defines what may and may not be claimed about ForgeOS v0.5.

## Verified claims

ForgeOS v0.5 includes 1,024 legacy typed outcome scaffolds, 62 deep Skill Contract v2 techniques, 62 evaluator bindings, 32 L0 kernel packages, 33 stable procedural providers, 234 candidate procedural providers, and 1,024 reference-only knowledge mappings. It includes a unified router, section materialization, global context compilation, deterministic skill-fabric primitives, Eval Lab v2, CLI/MCP parity, and the v0.4 production-oriented single-node Trust Kernel.

On the pinned public 16-case corpus, the router reaches Precision@1 93.75%, Precision@3 100%, Recall@6 100%, unsafe activation 0%, and deterministic repeatability 100%. The pinned context benchmark materializes 33/33 stable providers and demonstrates synthetic large-log and code-orientation reductions. These numbers apply only to the published corpus, estimator, fixtures, and release version.

## Claims that are not allowed

Do not claim:

- 1,024 deep or production-grade procedural skills;
- universal 70–90 percent token reduction;
- router superiority over every large skill framework;
- full PostgreSQL lifecycle or multi-node high availability;
- a universal third-party-code sandbox;
- 10,000 paired evaluation runs;
- certification by OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Microsoft, MCP, or A2A;
- perfect production readiness or zero defects.

## Open work

The major open targets are 192 core and 832 domain-specific procedural techniques, expanded hidden and multi-model evaluation, real tokenizer calibration, enriched Semantic ABI graphs, full PostgreSQL contract parity, sandboxed execution, organization identity provisioning, A2A streaming/push, and Studio graph editing.

## Public comparisons

ForgeOS may be compared with another project only on a pinned version, equal task/seed/model matrix, public methodology, disclosed hardware and cost, and reproducible evidence. Stars, repository size, or number of skill folders are not quality metrics.
